liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Spanish Jam** (3 reviews, 1 other source): Reviewer calls the Spanish Jam a highlight not to be missed; Spanish Jam is considered possibly the best of its era [3][8][10][12]
- **Clementine** (2 reviews): Reviewer rates this Clementine among the Dead's best, behind only a January 1969 version, citing its jazzy swing; Clementine is rated A+ and flows into New Potato Caboose and Born Cross Eyed [6][17]
- **Dark Star** (1 review, 1 other source): Dark Star is cut off, which is regretted; the very short Caution ends explosively, as if building toward something; Dark Star consists of only the first several notes [3][7]
- **New Potato Caboose** (1 review): Psychedelic Potato Caboose into Born Cross Eyed is called vintage and the reviewer's main reason for listening [11]
- **Born Cross Eyed** (1 review): The band slams into Born Cross Eyed relentlessly [13]
- **Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks)** (1 review): Short Caution jam drives along powerfully but fizzles out too early; it could have been great [10]

## Setlist highlights

- **Clementine**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 7 archived performances [18]
- **Born Cross Eyed**: rare: 14 archived performances [18]
- Earliest performances in the archive: Space [18]

## The recordings

- **gd68-01-20.sbd.jools.19470.sbe-fixed.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 7 songs; 33 min; rated 4.72/5 by 43 [1]. Said about its sound: Sounds very clear for the age of the tape; Recording quality is quite good for its age; vocals are minimal and are the one downside; Described as a crisp soundboard recording [7][12][17]
- **gd1968-01-20.sbd.miller.97340.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 6 songs; 33 min; rated 4.44/5 by 32 [2]
- **gd1968-01-20.sbd.ward.47.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 5 songs; 31 min; rated 4.2/5 by 5 [3]
- **gd1968-01-20.sbd.abe.4990.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 5 songs; 31 min; rated 4.2/5 by 5 [4]

## Around the show

- The tape is incomplete, which the reviewer finds tragic yet makes the available music more precious [13]
- DeadBase lists a Jam before Clementine; the tape reportedly starts on an announcer's remark; Feedback versus Space label is uncertain [1]
- Ranks this Clementine as arguably the best ever except for the 26 January 1969 one [6]
- Says Phil plays a Clementine part in the long Other One jam on 4/26/72, around 15-20 minutes in [10]
- This Clementine is judged much better than the 2/2/68 version on the So Many Roads box set [11]
- Listening in order, reviewer hears a sudden deepening, with the band sounding more like the Dead than before [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd68-01-20.sbd.jools.19470.sbe-fixed.shnf**: transferred by Julian (Jools) Elliott; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: This copy includes the short Dark Star at the end that the reviewer's older copy lacked; Dark Star ends earlier on some circulating tapes; the uploader's DAT cuts off early, while a cassette runs a minute or two longer [1][14]
- **gd1968-01-20.sbd.miller.97340.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> (4 Track) Master Reels -> Dat (44.1k) [2]. Also: Source is a DAT from Rob Eaton, with pitch correction help from Joe B. Jones [2]
- **gd1968-01-20.sbd.ward.47.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD -> MReel -> DAT -> CD-R [3]. Also: Broadcast on Grateful Dead Hour 342; not an FM recording [3]
- **gd1968-01-20.sbd.abe.4990.sbeok.shnf**: source: CD > EAC > SHN [4]

## Art and photos

- Photo by Zoooma (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead poster for 1/20/68 Municipal Auditorium, Eureka, California](https://www.flickr.com/photos/9692677@N07/2925190826/) [25]
- Photo by uncredited: [the page](https://www.flickr.com/photos/9692677@N07/2925190826/) [26]
